title: Two Sum (Sorted Array)
summary: Find if a pair of numbers in a sorted array sums to a target using two pointers to eliminate unnecessary pairs.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
Given a **sorted** array of integers `nums`, determine if there exists a pair of numbers that sum to a given `target`.

**Example 1:**
```
Input: nums = [1,3,4,6,8,10,13], target = 13
Output: True  # (3 + 10 = 13)
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input: nums = [1,3,4,6,8,10,13], target = 6
Output: False
```

sections.heading: Key Insight
sections.body:
Because the input is **sorted**, we can use two pointers starting at opposite ends to eliminate unnecessary pairs:

- If the current sum is **too large**, move the right pointer left (decreases the sum)
- If the current sum is **too small**, move the left pointer right (increases the sum)

Each pointer move eliminates an entire class of pairs that can't possibly work, achieving O(n) time with O(1) space.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
1. Initialize two pointers: `left` at index 0, `right` at the last index
2. While `left < right`:
   - Calculate `current_sum = nums[left] + nums[right]`
   - If `current_sum == target`, return `True`
   - If `current_sum < target`, increment `left` (need a larger sum)
   - If `current_sum > target`, decrement `right` (need a smaller sum)
3. If pointers meet without finding a pair, return `False`

approach: Initialize left pointer at index 0 and right pointer at the last index
Calculate the sum of elements at both pointers
If sum equals target, return True
If sum is less than target, move left pointer right to increase sum
If sum is greater than target, move right pointer left to decrease sum
Repeat until pointers meet; if no pair found, return False

quiz.q: Why does the two-pointer approach only work on a sorted array?
options: Because sorting reduces the time complexity to O(1)
Because we need the array length to be even
Because sortedness guarantees that moving a pointer changes the sum predictably in one direction
Because unsorted arrays cannot contain pairs that sum to a target
quiz.explain: In a sorted array, moving the left pointer right always increases the sum (larger value), and moving the right pointer left always decreases the sum (smaller value). This predictable behavior lets us eliminate half the search space with each move.

quiz.q: What is the space complexity of this two-pointer solution?
options: O(n) because we iterate through the array
O(log n) due to the pointer movements
O(1) because we only use two pointer variables
O(n²) because we consider all possible pairs
quiz.explain: We only use two integer variables (left and right pointers) regardless of input size, giving us constant O(1) space complexity. We don't create any additional data structures.
